negative_findings.description: Vijesti (vijesti.me), the largest independent Montenegrin daily and explicitly named in this coverage cell, did not surface a single article in any of seven searches, including two site-scoped local-language queries using its own domain and bank names.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only the homepage URL could be established. No economy-section path, article URL pattern, or feed was confirmed. Competing dailies (Dan) and portals (CdM, RTCG) surfaced normally on identical query shapes.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If Vijesti is systematically absent from the search index available to this run, keyword-based discovery will silently under-represent the outlet most likely to break bank-fee and supervision stories. Collection must be built by direct site crawl, not search.

negative_findings.description: Targeted queries for 'Portal Analitika' (portalanalitika.me) and 'Standard' (standard.co.me) as Montenegrin economy/banking outlets returned no direct hits.
negative_findings.result_summary: Neither outlet produced a confirmed URL or banking article in this run; one search summary explicitly noted the absence of Portal Analitika and Standard.co.me results.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Both are commonly cited Montenegrin portals. Their absence is more likely a search-coverage artefact than evidence they are inactive, so they should be probed directly rather than written off — recording them as candidates now would be fabrication.

negative_findings.description: Local-language searches on payment-fee increases and card pricing ('naknade banaka Crna Gora poskupljenje platne kartice') returned mostly regulator and bank-own material (CBCG fee-comparability pages, CKB general terms PDF, Prva banka card page) rather than press coverage.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only two genuine press items on fee increases were found (RTCG 'Banke povećale naknade i provizije'; MINA on fee and commission income), both dated rather than current.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Payment-fee changes are a core topic for this cell but Montenegrin media appear to cover them episodically, not systematically. Press monitoring alone will miss most fee events; it must be paired with the CBCG fee-comparability register and bank tariff pages, which sit outside this cell.

negative_findings.description: Ekonomist.me, described in reference material as a Podgorica-based finance/fintech magazine founded in 2014, could not be confirmed at a specific live URL in this run.
negative_findings.result_summary: The publication was described only via an encyclopedic entry; no article URL or homepage hit appeared in search results. The domain recorded on the candidate is inferred from the publication name and flagged as a hypothesis.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: It is potentially the only dedicated fintech/payments outlet in the market — the single most on-topic source for the payments half of the brief — so confirming or replacing it should be a priority in the verification pass.

negative_findings.description: No paywall, robots.txt, or terms-of-use check was performed on any candidate; access_status values are inferences from search snippets only.
negative_findings.result_summary: MINA's full wire service, eKapija premium items, and Bloomberg Adria are the three most likely to be gated, but none was tested. No fetch was attempted against any candidate in this run.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection-method recommendations assume open access. If MINA or eKapija are licence-gated, the effective early-signal channel narrows to Bankar.me, Investitor.me and RTCG, changing the collection design.

coverage_gaps.description: No Albanian-language Montenegrin media were searched or found, despite a significant Albanian-speaking population in Ulcinj/Malesija and MINA operating an Albanian service.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a follow-up pass with Albanian banking terms ('bankat në Mal të Zi', 'fitimi i bankave', 'tarifat bankare') against Montenegrin Albanian-language outlets and MINA's Albanian feed.

coverage_gaps.description: The cell found general and business press but no broadcast/video-first or podcast sources beyond RTCG's text site, and no social/professional channels (LinkedIn newsrooms, X accounts of bank PR desks and financial journalists) where appointments and deals often break first.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a pass over Montenegrin financial journalists' and bank communications teams' social accounts, plus RTCG/TV Vijesti/Prva TV business programme archives, to catch appointment and deal signals ahead of article publication.

coverage_gaps.description: Only RTCG and Monitor were found to offer deep, systematically addressable archives (numeric article ids; PDF back-issues). For most portals the historical depth and archive URL structure are unknown.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: For each retained portal, probe archive/pagination structure and sitemap.xml, and register Wayback Machine coverage as a fallback so a multi-year fee-and-earnings timeline can be reconstructed.

coverage_gaps.description: Press coverage found is heavily weighted to sector-level profit aggregates derived from CBCG data. Individual-bank annual reports, investor-relations material and AGM/shareholder items were barely represented in media coverage.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Treat this cell as an event and interpretation layer only; pair it with cells covering CBCG publications, the Montenegroberza listing disclosures and each bank's own newsroom for primary IR documents.

coverage_gaps.description: Substantial republication overlap was observed across CdM, Aktuelno, Kodex and Borba, much of it likely originating from the MINA wire, but the originating outlet could not be determined from search snippets.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build near-duplicate detection and first-seen timestamping across these portals so that credibility and latency scores attach to the originating source rather than the fastest republisher.

brief: Montenegro's banking press landscape is small, concentrated and highly derivative: two specialist portals — Bankar.me and Investitor.me — plus the public broadcaster RTCG carry almost all substantive bank-by-bank earnings, fee and licensing reporting, and they build it directly on CBCG data, typically weeks before any English-language pickup. The general dailies (Vijesti, Pobjeda, Dan) and the high-volume portals (CdM, Aktuelno, Borba, Kodex) add investigative angles and act as fast mirrors for bank and ministry press releases, with much of that copy apparently sourced from the MINA national wire, so first-seen timestamping and duplicate detection matter more here than raw source count. Local-language (sr) search was decisively more productive than English across every query pair, and RTCG's numeric article archive plus Monitor's PDF back-issues are the only two channels found that support genuine historical backfill of fee-change and profit timelines. Two caveats shape collection design: Vijesti — the outlet most likely to break supervision and fee stories — was invisible to search in this run and must be crawled directly, and payment-fee coverage is episodic enough that press monitoring alone will not catch tariff changes without pairing it against CBCG's fee-comparability register and the banks' own tariff pages.
